subject: Private offer: unified SKU bundling and channel margin pathing
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearwave.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@clearwave.io
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer inquiry — bundling & channel margin mechanics

Hi Marcus,

We're getting close to finalizing the vendor shortlist for our AI inference platform and I wanted to surface a couple of specific asks before we proceed to legal:

- We intend to purchase via AWS Private Offer (ClearWave has a preferred distributor, DataBridge). We need a single bundled SKU covering multi-region (us-west/us-east) capacity. Can Redwood produce a single SKU mapping for that bundle?
- Channel margin: DataBridge expects a reselling netback (passback) as part of the PO. We need clear options for how that can be handled (list-price offset vs rebate vs distributor invoicing).
- Compliance: send SOC 2 summary and any marketplace readiness evidence (list of docs) so our InfoSec can pre-clear.
- Timeline: target PO issuance by 11/20.

Can you share sample structures and the playbook you use for private offers + channel passback mechanics? If possible, include a one-page summary we can attach to the PO.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that's easier.

Best,
Olivia Barnes
VP Procurement, ClearWave Health

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearwave.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — bundling & channel margin mechanics

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely support a single bundled SKU for a multi-region private offer. Quick summary of next steps and options: 

1) SKU mapping and bundle: we will produce a single private-offer SKU that maps to the dedicated instance pool across both us-west and us-east. That SKU is scoped to committed vGPU-hours and can include soft regions for failover.

2) Channel passback mechanics (three standard options):
   - List-price offset (preferred by Finance): Redwood lists the full price in the private offer, and we provide an explicit chargeback line that reduces the net invoice to the distributor (or to you). Cleaner for marketplace reporting and avoids some rebate tax complexities.
   - Post-invoice rebate: Redwood bills the full amount, then issues a rebate to DataBridge per agreed timing. Works if distributor needs a cashflow trail but introduces reconciliation steps.
   - Distributor invoicing model: DataBridge invoices ClearWave and Redwood pays the distributor margin to DataBridge directly (requires reseller agreement).

Attached: marketplace-passback-options.pdf (one-page), data-request-sheet.xlsx (consumption profile + legal contacts).

Can you confirm: expected committed ARR and whether the distributor requires netback as percent-of-billed or a fixed per-SKU fee? If you can share the procurement form we’ll draft a proposed structure and a one-page summary for your PO.

Irene and Tessa — looping you for margin / legal impact and quick finance sizing.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Cloud Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

---

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearwave.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@clearwave.io, Samir Desai <samir.desai@data-bridge.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — bundling & channel margin mechanics

Thanks Marcus — that helps. A couple quick data points: 
- Expected committed ARR: ~$1.2M over 12 months (50% in year 1 consumption, ramping).
- DataBridge prefers a percent-of-billed netback; their contract references a 6–8% target.
- Attached is our procurement form for the PO (procurement-form-clearwave.pdf).

We can do a 30-minute call tomorrow 10am PT if that works for your team.

—Olivia

Attachment: procurement-form-clearwave.pdf

---

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: ClearWave passback recommendation

Marcus / Tessa — quick internal note before the call with ClearWave: 

- Finance prefers the list-price offset approach. It preserves Redwood's top-line reporting and keeps marketplace gross-to-net simpler; tax treatment is more straightforward in most jurisdictions.
- Proposed passback bands for this deal size: 7.5% netback on committed spend up to $1.0M, 5% on incremental usage beyond committed, with an early-adopter credit of $60k amortized across the first 3 months. The credit protects the distributor's margin while preserving Redwood's effective unit economics.
- If Legal signs off, we should also embed a reconciliation cadence (quarterly true-up) and require the distributor to provide invoices showing passback movement to ClearWave.

Attached: finance-passback-model.csv (simple NPV and gross-to-net outputs).

I think this structure will be acceptable to ClearWave and DataBridge based on prior deals — recommend we present the list-price offset + banded netback in the one-pager.

Irene
Director, Revenue Ops

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@clearwave.io>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@data-bridge.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — bundling & channel margin mechanics

Olivia / Samir — thanks for the fast turnaround and for looping DataBridge. Following our internal review, here is what Redwood proposes for the private offer PO and channel passback: 

Summary (one-line): single bundled SKU private offer (multi-region) with list-price offset passback and banded netback tiers to DataBridge — protects marketplace reporting and eases tax/rebate flows.

Details: 
- Committed ARR: $1.2M over 12 months (as provided).
- SKU: REDW-MULTI-1YR-DED-ALLREG (maps to committed vGPU-hours across us-west/us-east).
- Passback structure: list-price offset; 7.5% netback on committed spend up to $1.0M; 5% on overage. Early-adopter credit: $60,000 applied to month 1–3 invoices as a separate line item.
- Reconciliation: quarterly true-up; Redwood will provide a passback statement and expects DataBridge to provide distributor invoices to ClearWave for verification.
- Docs: attached proposed-private-offer-summary.pdf (one-pager), SOC2-Summary.pdf. We will follow with a draft private-offer in DocuSign once you confirm the structure and the procurement form is acceptable.

Next steps: 
1) Olivia — confirm acceptance of the banded netback and the early-adopter credit treatment.
2) Samir / DataBridge — confirm you can accept list-price offset on your side (we can do a short ops call if needed).
3) Once confirmed, Redwood will send a draft private offer + DocuSign link for PO signature.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654321
Draft PO (DocuSign): https://docusign.example.com/rw-clw-2026-0089

Thanks — happy to jump on the scheduled 10am PT call to walk through.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Cloud Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference
